The survey combines wordlists elicited during 1998 fieldwork with lists reused from earlier Bhil\-country, Dhule, Garasia, Dungra Bhil and Ahirani studies\. Source lexical\-similarity category numbers are retained only in Notes and do not assert historical cognacy\. English annotations are separated from phonetic forms; two literal unmatched open brackets remain preserved and explicitly flagged as uncertain\. Table 8 provides locality and administrative metadata but no point coordinates, so the thirty dialect records intentionally leave coordinates blank rather than inventing proxies\.

rows.gloss: stall-fed: cattle that do not go out grazing
rows.etymology: 1112. Chin. badehal, Pāḍ. bhadēl, Pāḍ. and Bhad. badhel ‘ox’ (Kaul [2006 i: 36] and [ii: 14], LSI [ix ,iv: 886]), and Kiũṭh. bhātalē ‘ox’ are partly cases of aspirated media ‘phoneme splitting’, discussed above p. 318. There are more cognates: Jaun. bhɔ̄d and bhōṭuṛɔ ‘bull’ (Z.) (both with fronted aspiration and the second form with -ṭuṛɔ suffix), Kiũṭh. bhātalē ‘oxen’ — Marw. bāldha gaḍḍi, Rj.jaip. bāldha gaḍḍī both ‘bullock cart’, Brj.- Aw. barad, baradh ‘ox’ — Mult. badhēlū ‘stall-fed: cattle that do not go out grazing’. NIA words like H. bail ‘ox’ are generally derived < OIA *balilla- ‘ox’ (9175). Under this lemma, Turner writes “Him. I 138: doubtful, as is also der. from *badhilla – ∼ badhirá – ‘deaf’.” But this is fact, as the quoted forms prove. It is difficult to imagine that these are loanwords of reconstructed OIA forms. Close to the Jaun. forms are Aw. barᵃdhā and Bagh. barᵃdā ‘bull’. Cf. also OIA balivárda- ‘ox, bull’ (9176) and its many reflexes. They resemble to some extend the here-quoted forms but are certainly not cognate. Also possible influence of OIA vádhri- ‘castrated’ (11256) is doubtful because of repeated meaning ‘bull’.
